To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the approximate solutions of the SLIP model, when used to predict the position and velocity trajectories of the monopedal robot, have average prediction errors of approximately 2% and approximately 7%, respectively.
the approximate solutions of the spring–mass models are accurate enough for practical applications in physical monopeds.

the feed-forward predictor for a monopod robot is capable of predicting position and velocity trajectories of the monopod robot with average prediction errors 2% and respectively 7%, and this predictor is capable of predicting the position and velocity of the monopedal robot in the presence of disturbances with average prediction errors less than 2% and less than 10%, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a feed-forward predictor for the monopedal spring-loaded inverted pendulm (SLIP) model.
the development and evaluation of a feed-forward predictor of the dynamics of a spring-loaded inverted pendular template for a planar monopedal robot.
the development and validation of a simple, yet powerful, analytical model of a planar monopedal robot, which can be used as a basis for control and estimation of such robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spring–mass model is a very good approximation to the monopedal dynamics and the predictor is a very good tool to use in practice.
the predictor is accurate enough for the control purposes.
the spring–mass models are a useful and practical tool for the analysis of monopod running, but only when their limitations are understood and accounted for.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the applicability of an analytical model for a physical robot.
the spring–mass dynamics can serve as a very accurate model for the physical system, and that the approximations can serve as the basis for a feedforward controller.
, we have developed a simple and accurate feed-forward predictor for a spring-mass model of a monopod robot.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spring-loaded inverted-pendulum template, and its approximate solutions, can be a useful tool in the development of monopedal locomotion systems, as well as a basis for the design of state estimators and controllers for these systems.
simple analytical models of running dynamics can be used with confidence to control physical robots.
, in spite of its simplicity, the spring-loaded inverted-pendulum (SLIP) model can be an accurate predictor for the monopedal locomotion of physical robots, as long as it is properly parameterized.
